'''European Women in Mathematics (EWM)''' is an international association of women working in the field of mathematics in Europe. The association participates in political and strategic work to promote the role of women in mathematics and offers its members direct support. Its goals include encouraging women to study mathematics and providing visibility to women mathematicians. It is the "first and best known" of several organizations devoted to women in mathematics in Europe.<ref>{{citation|first=Caroline|last=Series|authorlink=Caroline Series|title=European Level Organisations for Women Mathematicians|url=http://www.ems-ph.org/journals/newsletter/pdf/2013-12-90.pdf|magazine=EMS Newsletter|publisher=European Mathematical Society|volume=90|date=December 2013|page=11}}</ref>

== Mission ==
European Women in Mathematics aims to encourage women to study mathematics, support women in their careers, provide a meeting place for like-minded people and highlight and make women mathematicians visible. In this way, and by promoting scientific communication and working with groups and organisations with similar goals, they spread their vision of mathematics and science.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Mission – European Women in Mathematics|url=https://www.europeanwomeninmaths.org/about-us/mission/|access-date=2020-11-01|language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Mentorship ===
EWM has a mentoring programme which can be joined at any time of the year. EWM brings together a younger and a more experienced member to share different experiences and perspectives for motivation and inspiration.

=== Grants ===
EWM awards travel grants for female mathematicians every year. The travel grants are awarded to EWM members who are at an early stage of their career or work in a developing country and who need financial resources (travel and/or accommodation, up to 400 EUR) to attend and speak at an important conference in their field of expertise.

== Regular Activities ==
Every other year, EWM holds a general meeting and a summer school. A newsletter is published at least twice a year, EWM has a website, a Facebook group and an e-mail network. EWM coordinates a mentoring programme and awards a travel grant twice a year.

=== General Meetings ===
EWM hold a General Meeting every other year in the form of a week-long conference with a scientific program of mini-courses on mathematical topics, discussions on the situation of women in the field and a General Assembly.

General meetings have been held in Paris (1986), Copenhagen (1987), Warwick (1988), Lisbon (1990), Marseilles (1991), Warsaw (1993),<ref name="update">{{citation|last=Series|first=Caroline|title=European Women in Mathematics Update|date=March 1996|url=http://www.emis.de/newsletter/19/EMS19-2.ps|magazine=EMS Newsletter|volume=19|publisher=[[European Mathematical Society]]|accessdate=2018-09-17|authorlink=Caroline Series|via=[[American Mathematical Society]]}}</ref> Madrid (1995),<ref name="update" /> Trieste ICTP (1997), Hannover (1999),  Malta (2001), Luminy (2003), Volgograd (2005), Cambridge (2007),<ref>{{Cite web|first=|date=2015-09-23|title=EWM 2007, Cambridge|url=https://www.maths.cam.ac.uk/women-mathematics/ewm-2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180831002427/https://www.maths.cam.ac.uk/women-mathematics/ewm-2007|archive-date=2018-08-31|access-date=2018-08-30|website=[[University of Cambridge]], Faculty of Mathematics|language=en|url-status=dead}}</ref> Novi Sad (2009),<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=2009-08-25|title=Math Up! 14th general meeting of European Women in Mathematics (EWM). Novi Sad (Serbia), 25–28 August 2009|url=http://www.unesco.org/new/en/venice/about-this-office/single-view/news/math_up_14th_general_meeting_of_european_women_in_mathemati/|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2018-08-30|website=[[UNESCO]]|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{citation|last=Praeger|first=Cheryl E.|title='Oh no. A woman doing mathematics!'|date=November 2009|url=http://www.austms.org.au/Publ/Gazette/2009/Nov09/CommsPraeger.pdf|journal=Gazette of the Australian Mathematical Society|pages=324–329|authorlink=Cheryl Praeger}}</ref> Barcelona (2011), Bonn (2013), Cortona (2015), and Graz (2018).<ref name=":0" />

===Activities at international conferences=== 
EWM holds satellite conferences to the European Congress in Mathematics and takes part in ICWM International Conference of Women in Mathematics, International Congress of Women Mathematicians and now World Meeting for Women Mathematicians.

== History ==
Although the group that became EWM began holding informal meetings as early as 1974,<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Greenwald | first1 = Sarah J.
 | last2 = Leggett | first2 = Anne M. | author2-link = Anne M. Leggett
 | last3 = Thomley | first3 = Jill E.
 | doi = 10.1007/s00283-015-9539-8
 | issue = 3
 | journal = The Mathematical Intelligencer
 | mr = 3406282
 | pages = 11–21
 | title = The Association for Women in Mathematics: how and why it was founded, and why it's still needed in the 21st century
 | volume = 37
 | year = 2015}}</ref>
EWM was founded as an organization in 1986 by [[Bodil Branner]], [[Caroline Series]], [[Gudrun Kalmbach]], [[Marie-Françoise Roy]], and [[Dona Strauss]], inspired by the activities of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] in the USA.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www-history.mcs.st-andrews.ac.uk/Societies/European_Women.html|title=European Women in Mathematics|last=|first=|date=February 2018|website=[[MacTutor History of Mathematics archive]]|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2018-08-30}}</ref> It was established as an association under Finnish law in 1993 with its seat in Helsinki.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{citation
 | last = Näätänen | first = Marjatta
 | contribution = A brief history of the EWM office in Helsinki, 1991–2001
 | date = March 2003
 | doi = 10.1142/9789812704276_0001
 | publisher = World Scientific
 | title = European Women in Mathematics: Proceedings of the Tenth General Meeting}}</ref>
In fact, the basic structure defining the convenor, standing committee and coordinators was established between 1987 and 1991. An EWM email net was set up in 1994 followed by a web page in 1997.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.europeanwomeninmaths.org/about-us/history/|title=History – European Women in Mathematics|language=en-US|access-date=2019-10-08}}</ref>

The organization has a Scientific Committee, jointly with the [[European Mathematical Society]] and its Committee on Women in Mathematics.

== Similar Societies ==
There are many similar societies like the "European Women in Mathematics" society that celebrate women in Mathematics.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.europeanwomeninmaths.org/about-us/similar-societies/|title=Similar Societies – European Women in Mathematics|language=en-US|access-date=2019-10-08}}</ref> For instance:

=== Women in Mathematics ===
*[[International Mathematical Union]] (IMU) Committee for Women in Mathematics<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mathunion.org/cwm|title=CWM {{!}} International Mathematical Union (IMU)|website=www.mathunion.org|access-date=2019-10-08}}</ref>
*EMS Women in Mathematics Committee<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://euro-math-soc.eu/committee/women|title=Women|website=euro-math-soc.eu|language=en|access-date=2019-10-08}}</ref>
*EMS/EWM Scientific Committee<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://womenandmath.wordpress.com/emsewm-scientific-committee/|title=EMS/EWM Scientific Committee|date=2008-03-22|website=Women and Mathematics|language=en|access-date=2019-10-08}}</ref>
*Femmes et mathématiques<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.femmes-et-maths.fr/|title=Femmes et Mathématiques|website=www.femmes-et-maths.fr|access-date=2019-10-08}}</ref>
*EWM - The Netherlands <ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ewmnetherlands.nl/|title=EWM - The Netherlands|website=www.ewmnetherlands.nl|access-date=2021-07-08}}</ref>
*LMS Women in Mathematics Committee<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/about/committees/women-mathematics-committee|title=Women in Mathematics Committee {{!}} London Mathematical Society|website=www.lms.ac.uk|access-date=2019-10-08}}</ref>

*[[:pl:Polskie Towarzystwo Kobiet w Matematyce|Polish Woman in Mathematics]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=Contact |date=2021-06-08 |title=Polish Women in Mathematics |url=https://ptkwm.pl/en/contact/ |access-date=2025-02-19 |language=en-GB}}</ref>
